correctness.rationale: The corner-unit argument forces every nonzero vertex coefficient to entail its full primitive idempotent; Peirce projections separate surviving arrow corners. Their arbitrary independent subspaces give a bijection and exact graded count. Gaussian polynomial exponents r(m-r) yield the coefficientwise O(q^-1) leading law, with full justification of positivity and the multiplicity-two threshold. Thirteen direct full-subspace ideal enumerations agree, while finite checks are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The theorem determines the natural full ideal quotient-dimension enumerator for every finite quiver, including loops and arbitrary parallel arrows, and recovers a complete lattice inclusion criterion. Beyond the standard local Gaussian count, it gives a sharp field-dependence boundary and a nontrivial all-quiver large-field probability law, with a three-vertex model producing three equiprobable quotient dimensions. These natural invariants support ideal-lattice enumeration and quiver comparisons without per-ideal search.
